candidates.title: GenAI-supported self-explanation and its effects on metacognitive monitoring and critical reading comprehension: evidence from two experimental studies
candidates.reason: Study 1 compared self-explanation plus personalized GenAI feedback, self-explanation alone and reading only among 119 students. Study 2 compared scaffolded, standard and no prompts among 113 students. The studies separate immediate comprehension, explanation quality, monitoring accuracy and reported cognitive load.
candidates.source_comparison: Feedback improved immediate critical-reading comprehension in Study 1, but not absolute monitoring accuracy. Scaffolded prompts improved explanation quality and monitoring accuracy in Study 2, but not critical-reading comprehension. No delayed or independent-transfer test was administered.

candidates.title: Cognitive load theory and learner competencies as predictors of effective GenAI training for preservice teachers
candidates.reason: A convenience sample of 450 preservice teachers in Spain and Indonesia reported cognitive load, prior knowledge, metacognitive and problem-solving skills, and perceived usefulness while designing GenAI-supported materials.
candidates.source_comparison: The model concerns perceived load and usefulness, not objectively measured load, teaching performance or a training effect. Its cross-sectional paths do not establish the causal language used in the model description.

candidates.title: Why Teacher AI Use Has Plateaued, and What Could Come Next
candidates.reason: A nationally representative EdWeek Research Center survey of 590 teachers found 62% reported at least some classroom AI use, compared with 61% in 2025. The article distinguishes the measured plateau from experts' explanations about saturation, screen-time concerns, guidance and training.

candidates.title: What Happens When AI Outruns Title I Schools?
candidates.reason: A Title I high-school teacher argues that unclear rules, uneven tool access and insufficient training leave teachers giving students contradictory messages about using AI as a thought partner rather than a generator.
candidates.qualification: The school examples and proposed seven-step plan are the author's experience and argument, not measured outcomes.

candidates.title: Is AI-assisted thinking devaluing business degrees?
candidates.reason: Directly concerns which thinking and judgment a degree is meant to develop, but the original article still needs an independent full read before synthesis.

candidates.title: US schools are moving away from AI in Google searches. Should Australia do the same?
candidates.reason: Potentially relevant to search, source evaluation and attention, but the exact argument and examples remain to be checked against the full article.
